action_items: (CRITICAL) Debug why /welcome unconditionally redirects to /login. Verified: localStorage is empty (no lore_token, no lore_user), AuthContext should set user=null, Landing's `if (user)` branch should NOT fire. No explicit nav('/login') exists in Landing.jsx or App.js for path '/welcome'. Suggest: (a) add console.log inside Landing.jsx render to confirm component mounts; (b) check whether Landing component has a runtime error causing React Router to fall through to '*' → '/' → RootRedirect; (c) verify the export default in Landing.jsx; (d) try removing the `if (user) { setTimeout(...) }` line — it runs as a side-effect during render which is an anti-pattern and could trigger weird behavior under StrictMode. Replace with useEffect.

rca of the issue: Symptom: GET /welcome → URL rewrites to /login, Auth.jsx renders. Repro: clear localStorage (or open private/fresh context), goto /welcome. Hypothesis: Landing.jsx line 9 `if (user) { setTimeout(() => nav('/home'), 0); }` is a render-time side effect. While `user` is null on initial render, in React StrictMode (CRA dev default) double-render + memoized auth context value could cause an unintended branch. More likely: Landing component throws/errors silently, React Router falls to wildcard '*' → '/' → RootRedirect → '/welcome' loop, eventually some child Auth render wins. Suggest: (1) wrap Landing.jsx body in try/catch + console.log to confirm it mounts; (2) move setTimeout into useEffect; (3) remove the `if (user)` redirect entirely (RootRedirect at '/' already handles this — visiting /welcome while logged in is fine, just show Landing).
